categories.main_business_segments: STAG Industrial, Inc. operates as a single business segment focused on the acquisition, ownership, and operation of industrial properties across the United States. The company manages its operations on an aggregated, single segment basis for performance assessment and reporting purposes.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: STAG's core business relies on a fully integrated platform for property acquisition, leasing, and management, leveraging proprietary risk assessment models and quantitative analysis to identify and underwrite industrial real estate investments. The company emphasizes disciplined investment, property management, and operational efficiency, with a focus on maintaining high occupancy and asset quality.
categories.primary_customers_markets: STAG serves a diversified base of tenants across a wide range of industries, including air freight & logistics, containers & packaging, automobile components, machinery, and commercial services. Its properties are primarily leased to companies involved in distribution, logistics, manufacturing, and related industrial activities, with no single tenant accounting for more than 2.9% of annualized base rental revenue and no single industry exceeding 11.3%.
categories.geographic_coverage: STAG owns 591 buildings totaling approximately 116.6 million rentable square feet in 41 states across the U.S., with its top markets including Chicago, Greenville, Minneapolis, Pittsburgh, Detroit, Columbus, and Philadelphia. The portfolio is geographically diversified, with the top 20 markets accounting for 58.4% of total annualized base rental revenue.
categories.supply_chain_position: STAG operates as an owner and lessor of industrial real estate, positioning itself downstream in the supply chain by providing critical infrastructure (warehouses, distribution centers, and light manufacturing facilities) to tenants engaged in logistics, distribution, and production.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic priorities include disciplined growth through individual and small portfolio acquisitions, maintaining a diversified tenant and geographic mix, and enhancing shareholder value via sustainable long-term growth in distributable cash flow. STAG also integrates ESG initiatives into its business strategy, with published sustainability goals and participation in industry benchmarks such as GRESB.
categories.revenue_model: STAG generates revenue primarily through rental income from leasing industrial properties to tenants under triple net, modified gross, and gross lease structures. The majority of leases are triple net, passing most operating expenses to tenants, and revenue is recognized on a straight-line basis over lease terms.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: STAG competes with national, regional, and local owners and operators of industrial real estate, including both public and private REITs and institutional investors. Its differentiated strategy focuses on granular, nationwide acquisitions in Tier 1 industrial markets, providing diversification versus competitors who concentrate in super-primary markets.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2024, STAG had total assets of $6.8 billion, annual rental income of $762.9 million, and net income of $193.3 million. The company’s same store operating revenue grew 4.5% year-over-year, and it continues to expand through acquisitions, with $710 million in property acquisitions in 2024 and a portfolio occupancy rate of 96.5%.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: STAG emphasizes a diversified, risk-managed portfolio of high-quality industrial assets, offering reliable cash flow, geographic and tenant diversification, and access to a broad set of acquisition opportunities. Its focus on single-asset and small portfolio acquisitions, combined with disciplined underwriting and strong balance sheet management, positions it as a stable, long-term investment vehicle for shareholders seeking exposure to U.S. industrial real estate.
